  • Method Details

    • singleQuoted

      static String singleQuoted(String value)
      Wraps a string value in SQL single quotes, escaping any embedded single quotes by doubling them.

      Example: singleQuoted("it's") → "'it''s'".

      Parameters:
      value - string to quote; must not be null
      Returns:
      SQL single-quoted string literal

    • literalFromDate

      static String literalFromDate(Date date)
      Formats a Date value as a SQL TIMESTAMP literal.

      The returned string has the form TIMESTAMP 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS' using Locale.ROOT so that the output is locale-independent.

      Parameters:
      date - date/time value; must not be null
      Returns:
      SQL TIMESTAMP literal string

    • getFingerprint

      static List<?> getFingerprint(Iterable<?>... values)
      Copies one or more ordered sequences of values into a stable List suitable for use as a hash key.

      Each sequence becomes one element of the result rather than being flattened into it, so that a key records which sequence every value came from. Flattening would let different groupings of the same values collide — a property list of ["a"] with criteria ["b"] against a property list of ["a", "b"] with no criteria — and a cache keyed that way would answer one with a statement generated for the other.

      Parameters:
      values - zero or more iterables whose contents form the fingerprint
      Returns:
      one list per sequence, in order, each holding that sequence's values

    • coerce

      static Object coerce(Class<?> type, Object value)
      Converts a value read from the database to a target Java type.

      Drivers are free to return whatever representation they please for a column — any Number subtype for a numeric column, text for a character one — so a value that already fits its target is returned untouched and anything else is narrowed to it.

      Parameters:
      type - target type; may be primitive
      value - value to convert; may be null
      Returns:
      value as type, or unchanged when no conversion applies

    • getAllBeanProperties

      static Iterable<PropertyDescriptor> getAllBeanProperties(Class<?> entityClass)
      Returns all readable bean properties for an entity type and its full superclass hierarchy (excluding Object).

      Properties are collected from the top of the hierarchy downward so that subclass overrides shadow superclass definitions. The class property is always excluded. Only properties with a getter are included.

      An interface has no superclass, so its hierarchy is the interface alone; inherited properties are still reported, because bean introspection walks an interface's extended interfaces itself.

      Parameters:
      entityClass - entity class or interface; must not be null
      Returns:
      ordered list of readable property descriptors

    • resolveSqlType

      static Class<?> resolveSqlType(Class<?> javaType, jakarta.persistence.Column column)
      Determines the JDBC-compatible Java type to use for a named property when binding SQL parameters or reading result sets.

      When the property's getter carries a Column annotation with a non-blank columnDefinition, the SQL type keyword is inspected:

      • Contains CHAR → String
      • Starts with INT → Long
      • Starts with NUMBER, NUMERIC, or DECIMAL → Number
      • Equals DATE → Date
      • Equals TIME → Time
      • Equals or contains TIMESTAMP or equals DATETIME → Timestamp
      • Equals CLOB or TEXT → char[]
      • Anything else → Object

      When no column definition is present, the property type is returned after autoboxing any primitive via autobox(Class).

      Parameters:
      javaType - declared type of the mapped property or field
      column - column
      Returns:
      Java type to use for the SQL column

    • getAllDeclaredFields

      static Iterable<Field> getAllDeclaredFields(Class<?> entityClass)
      Returns every instance field declared by an entity type and its superclasses.

      Collected from the top of the hierarchy downward, so that a subclass field shadows one of the same name it hides. Static fields are constants rather than state, and synthetic fields are compiler bookkeeping, so neither is included. An interface declares no instance fields at all.

      Parameters:
      entityClass - entity class or interface; must not be null
      Returns:
      ordered instance fields, superclass declarations first

    • accessible

      static Field accessible(Field field)
      Suppresses access checks on a field so that it can be read and written regardless of its declared visibility.

      A field-mapped column is normally private with no accessor, which is the point of mapping it directly; reaching it requires the same suppression a JPA provider performs, and the same opens directive from a modular application.

      Parameters:
      field - field to make accessible
      Returns:
      the same field

    • getAnnotation

      @SafeVarargs static <A extends Annotation> A getAnnotation(Class<A> annotationType, AnnotatedElement... elements)
      Reads an annotation from the first of several elements that carries it.

      Lets a mapping be declared on a getter or on the field behind it, resolved in the order the caller considers authoritative. null elements are skipped, so a caller need not know which of them exist.

      Type Parameters:
      A - annotation type
      Parameters:
      annotationType - annotation to look for
      elements - elements to search, in precedence order; entries may be null
      Returns:
      the annotation from the first element carrying it, or null

    • getPropertyAnnotation

      static <A extends Annotation> A getPropertyAnnotation(Class<?> entityClass, PropertyDescriptor property, Class<A> annotationType)
      Reads a mapping annotation from a property, accepting it on either the getter or the backing field.

      Used to decide whether a property is mapped at all, for which either member carrying the annotation is enough; which of them wins when both do is ColumnMetaData's to resolve, since there it also decides how the column is accessed. Annotating the field is the more common style: it keeps the mapping beside the state it describes and leaves plain accessors uncluttered.

      Type Parameters:
      A - annotation type
      Parameters:
      entityClass - entity class or interface declaring the property
      property - property to read the annotation from; must have a getter
      annotationType - annotation to look for
      Returns:
      the annotation from the getter, else from the backing field, else null

    • appendCorrelation

      static boolean appendCorrelation(StringBuilder sb, String outerAlias, String subAlias, Iterable<String> idColumnNames)
      Appends correlated subAlias.col = outerAlias.col predicates for each column name, joined by AND.

      When idColumnNames is empty the buffer is unchanged and false is returned.

      Parameters:

      outerAlias - alias of the outer query's table reference
      subAlias - alias of the correlated subquery's table reference
      idColumnNames - column names to correlate
      Returns:
